item.vignette: A child with Alagille syndrome and severe cholestatic pruritus starts maralixibat. Fecal bile acid loss increases and serum bile acid concentrations fall.
item.lead_in: Which transport process is directly inhibited?

options.A: Apical sodium-dependent bile acid reuptake in the terminal ileum
options.B: Canalicular bile salt export from hepatocytes
options.C: Basolateral uptake of bile acids into hepatocytes by NTCP

item.tested_construct: Reversible inhibition of the ileal bile acid transporter, reducing enterohepatic bile acid reabsorption
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among plausible pharmacologic targets; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: Maralixibat reversibly inhibits the ileal bile acid transporter (IBAT), decreasing reabsorption of bile acids from the terminal ileum and thereby reducing enterohepatic recirculation.

distractor_explanations.A: Correct. IBAT mediates apical bile acid reuptake in the terminal ileum.
distractor_explanations.B: BSEP mediates canalicular bile salt export and is not inhibited by maralixibat.
distractor_explanations.C: NTCP mediates hepatic sinusoidal bile acid uptake rather than ileal reabsorption.
distractor_explanations.D: MDR3 transports phospholipids into bile and is not the direct target.
distractor_explanations.E: MRP2 transports conjugated bilirubin and other organic anions, not the target of maralixibat.

explanation.educational_objective: Link IBAT inhibition in the terminal ileum with reduced enterohepatic bile acid recycling and lower circulating bile acids.

item.vignette: An adolescent with homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia has minimal functional LDL receptors. After treatment with evinacumab-dgnb, LDL cholesterol decreases substantially despite the receptor defect.
item.lead_in: Which circulating protein is directly neutralized?
item.tested_construct: Neutralization of ANGPTL3 with LDL-receptor-independent enhancement of lipoprotein processing
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among plausible pharmacologic targets; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: Evinacumab-dgnb is a monoclonal antibody that binds and inhibits ANGPTL3. ANGPTL3 normally inhibits lipoprotein lipase and endothelial lipase; its blockade promotes lipoprotein processing and can lower LDL cholesterol independently of LDL-receptor function.

distractor_explanations.A: PCSK9 inhibition depends on preserved LDL-receptor recycling and is less effective when LDLR function is absent.
distractor_explanations.C: Apolipoprotein B is not the direct antibody target.
distractor_explanations.D: CETP inhibition alters cholesterol transfer between lipoproteins but is not the mechanism of evinacumab.
distractor_explanations.E: ANGPTL4 also regulates lipoprotein lipase but is not the direct target of evinacumab.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize ANGPTL3 inhibition as an LDL-receptor-independent lipid-lowering mechanism.

item.vignette: An adult with severe hemophilia A receives a one-time AAV5-based gene therapy. Months later, liver-derived expression of a therapeutic coagulation protein is detectable and factor activity has increased.
item.lead_in: Which transgene product is being expressed?
item.tested_construct: Hepatic expression of a B-domain-deleted human factor VIII transgene
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among plausible pharmacologic targets; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: Valoctocogene roxaparvovec-rvox is an AAV5-based gene therapy that delivers a transgene encoding the B-domain-deleted SQ form of human factor VIII. Transcription occurs in the liver and produces circulating factor VIII activity.

distractor_explanations.A: Factor IX replacement is used for hemophilia B, not hemophilia A.
distractor_explanations.B: Von Willebrand factor stabilizes factor VIII but is not the transgene encoded by this therapy.
distractor_explanations.C: Correct. The vector encodes a B-domain-deleted human factor VIII transgene.
distractor_explanations.D: Activated factor VII is used as a bypassing agent rather than the encoded gene product.
distractor_explanations.E: Factor XI is unrelated to the deficient protein in hemophilia A.

explanation.educational_objective: Connect AAV5 liver-directed gene transfer in hemophilia A with expression of a B-domain-deleted factor VIII transgene.

item.vignette: A patient with BCG-unresponsive non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer receives an intravesical non-replicating adenoviral vector. Several days later, interferon-alfa 2b protein is detectable in the urine.
item.lead_in: Which event most directly explains this finding?

options.A: Selective lysis of urothelial cells by replicating adenovirus
options.B: Systemic secretion of interferon by hepatocytes
options.C: Activation of endogenous bladder interferon genes by CRISPR editing
options.D: Transduction of urothelial cells with transient local expression of an interferon-alfa 2b transgene
options.E: Release of interferon from intravesical BCG organisms

item.tested_construct: Adenoviral transduction of bladder urothelium with transient local IFN-alfa 2b expression
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among plausible pharmacologic targets; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: Nadofaragene firadenovec-vncg is a non-replicating adenoviral vector designed to deliver a human interferon-alfa 2b gene to bladder urothelial cells. Intravesical administration produces local cell transduction and transient expression of IFN-alfa 2b.

distractor_explanations.A: The vector is non-replicating and is not intended to kill cells through viral replication.
distractor_explanations.B: Expression is localized to the bladder urothelium rather than driven by hepatic secretion.
distractor_explanations.C: The therapy delivers a transgene and does not edit the endogenous interferon locus with CRISPR.
distractor_explanations.D: Correct. Urothelial transduction produces transient local IFN-alfa 2b expression.
distractor_explanations.E: BCG is not the source of the detected interferon protein after this gene therapy.

explanation.educational_objective: Differentiate local adenoviral transgene expression from replicating viral therapy, systemic cytokine delivery, and genome editing.

item.vignette: A patient with erosive esophagitis receives vonoprazan. Gastric acid secretion falls rapidly even though the drug does not require activation in an acidic canaliculus.
item.lead_in: Which molecular action most directly accounts for this effect?

options.A: Irreversible covalent inhibition of the gastric H+/K+-ATPase after acid activation
options.B: Competitive blockade of histamine H2 receptors
options.D: Inhibition of carbonic anhydrase in parietal cells
options.E: Reversible potassium-competitive inhibition of the gastric H+/K+-ATPase

item.tested_construct: Reversible potassium-competitive inhibition of the gastric proton pump
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among plausible pharmacologic targets; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: Vonoprazan suppresses gastric acid secretion by inhibiting the H+/K+-ATPase in a potassium-competitive manner. It binds active proton pumps noncovalently and reversibly and does not require acid activation.

distractor_explanations.A: Conventional proton-pump inhibitors require acid activation and form covalent bonds; vonoprazan does not.
distractor_explanations.B: H2-receptor antagonists reduce histamine signaling upstream rather than directly inhibiting the proton pump.
distractor_explanations.C: Antacids neutralize secreted acid but do not inhibit the parietal-cell proton pump.
distractor_explanations.D: Carbonic anhydrase contributes to acid generation but is not the direct target.
distractor_explanations.E: Correct. Vonoprazan is a reversible potassium-competitive inhibitor of the gastric H+/K+-ATPase.

explanation.educational_objective: Differentiate potassium-competitive acid blockade from covalent proton-pump inhibition, H2 blockade, and antacid therapy.
